title: #badcinderella
transcript: The reviews for Bad Cinderella are out, and they're not surprising, but it's fascinating and I want to talk about it a little bit. Haven't seen this production. All I know is everything I've heard online, which has been a lot. And it's fascinating also because this, to me, harkens back to the mega musicals of the 90s and 80s, meaning it's a large scale musical that's transferred from the West End to Broadway. And it's Android Webber. I mean, it's not totally a mega musical as we think about, but in a lot of ways it is. And it's one of, I think the last anyway. So what's fascinating to me is that everyone who seen the show that I know and I trust their opinion has all kind of said the same thing. But this wasn't so much bad as it was a total misfire and it was kind of boring and. And also didn't really make sense. And I could even see that just looking at the press clips. I'm like, who is this Cinderella? She's bad, but she's, like, against the patriarchy. I don't know what's going on here. And she's against, like, beauty standards, but then she becomes beautiful at one point. I don't. It doesn't make any sense. My point is, if so many people saw this and walked away with kind of the same feelings, the feelings that were represented in most of the reviews that came out today, how come no one on The creative team did anything about it. And you could argue that a lot of it is Andrews ego perhaps, and they just wanted to like placate him and like do what he asked for. But I also really feel that Andrew is really sensitive about critics responses and he wants to have a hit. So what went so vastly wrong that so many people could clearly see the problem and the reviews reflected what those people were saying and seeing and nothing was done to address it? This isn't like a movie or TV show where it shot, it's released and there it is. This is a living, breathing thing that they could have adapted and it really fix some of these problems that just don't make sense. So it's, it's I. I don't understand how it got to this point. And this is nothing to do with the performers and the creative team, who all do their jobs and apparently are doing them very well. It's the people who structure the show. How come that wasn't fixed? How come this, how come what everyone agreed was a problem, that's all the show, the people who are actually in charge of fixing the problem, didn't do it?
